content.text:
I fitted the two spin-allowed bands first to get Dq and B. I then set C so that the calculated ¹E level matches the 9 748 cm⁻¹ band.

**1. Dq and B from the spin-allowed bands (³T₁g(F) ground state)**

Let Δ = 10Dq. For d² in an octahedral field:
- ν(³T₂) = Δ/2 − 7.5B + ½√(Δ² + 18ΔB + 225B²)
- ν(³T₁(P)) = √(Δ² + 18ΔB + 225B²)

Setting ν(³T₁(P)) = 25 000 cm⁻¹ gives ν(³T₂) = Δ/2 − 7.5B + 12 500 = 17 500 cm⁻¹. That rearranges to **Δ = 10 000 + 15B**.

Substituting this into the second equation:
- 10⁸ + 480 000B + 720B² = 6.25×10⁸
- Solving the quadratic gives **B = 583.3 cm⁻¹**.
- Then Δ = 18 750 cm⁻¹, so **Dq = 1875 cm⁻¹**.

**2. C from the spin-forbidden ¹E band**

The ¹E level depends on C as well as Dq and B, so I diagonalised the full d² ligand-field matrices with Dq = 1875 cm⁻¹ and B = 583.3 cm⁻¹, trying two values of C:

| C (cm⁻¹) | E(¹E) (cm⁻¹) |
|---|---|
| 2333 | 8 556 |
| 2950 | 9 790 |

E(¹E) goes up by about 2 cm⁻¹ for every 1 cm⁻¹ increase in C. Interpolating to 9 748 cm⁻¹ gives **C ≈ 2930 cm⁻¹**, so C/B ≈ 5.0. I did not run a final check at that exact value. As a check on Dq and B, both runs give ³T₂ at exactly 17 500 cm⁻¹ and ³T₁(P) at exactly 25 000 cm⁻¹. ³A₂ comes out at 36 250 cm⁻¹. The fitted B is well below the free-ion value for V³⁺ (about 860 cm⁻¹), which points to a fairly covalent metal–ligand bond.
